Handling different fabric width within the same Style BOM for Order/

# Section 1: Overview

# Purpose
This document describes the business requirement for handling situations where the required fabric width is partially unavailable from the supplier and alternate fabric widths are supplied. This case can also arise due to different width planned to procure to gain better fabric utilization efficiency. The system should support updating BOM fabric width details and allow manual adjustment of fabric consumption accordingly in line with available sales order colors and Sizes quantities.
This should handle both Sizes and Size groups.

# Business Requirement
In garment manufacturing, BOM consumption is calculated based on a predefined fabric width (for example 50”). However, suppliers may not always provide the complete required quantity in the same width.
Example:
- Required Fabric Width: 50”
- Required Quantity: 1000 Meters
- Supplier Availability:
• 600 Meters in 50”
• Remaining 400 Meters in 52”
In such cases, the BOM must reflect actual suppliable widths, and fabric consumption needs manual adjustment because consumption varies based on width.

Currently, the ERP system supports only a single width per BOM line and does not provide flexibility to manage mixed-width procurement scenarios against individual material line.

# Section 2. Assumptions

# Assumptions
• No Assumptions

# Section 3. Solution

# Functional Requirement.

## Option to define multiple fabric widths against same BOM Line
There will be a new option to define consumptions and Prices based on Fabric colors and widths as shown below.
There will be a new link on Material BOM line as highlighted below.

##### BOM Material line
Figure 1 – Bom Material Line
Upon click on this link, system will open below screen where user will be able to select Material Color, Size (width) and will be able to enter consumptions & prices against garment sizes, and multiple Sizes of material, if required.
On this screen, the user can edit Consumption and Price, and the values automatically populate back onto the color/size-wise screen. When individual fabric widths and sizes are added separately, the highest value is automatically populated on the Material tab screen. This should be handled through permission “”.
This grid will also have option to define material consumption & Price against Size groups.

##### Using Individual Sizes:
In case user wants to enter material consumption and prices based on Garment Color, Garment Sizes, Material Color and Material Sizes then user can enter those details using size and color Dependencies and there are five color dependencies and four size dependencies.

### Color Dependency
• Base Color
• Matching
• Body Type
• Table
• None

### Size Dependency
• Base Size
• Fabric Width
• Table
• None
Combining the five Color Dependency options with the four Size Dependency options gives many possible ways of applying fabric consumption and price. Each combination is detailed below, together with a screenshot of the corresponding screen.

### 1. Base Color / Base Size
Material color and material size mirror the garment color and size directly, so no separate mapping is required. In this combination, the user can also add the fabric consumption and price.
Figure 2 – Base Color / Base Size

### 2. Base Color / Table
The user can define fabric width and price for each combination of material size and base color. This table view allows a different fabric width and price to be set for every garment size and base color.
Figure 3 – Base Color / Table

### 3. Base Color / None
The user defines a fabric width consumption, and price for each base color, with no dependency on garment size.
Figure 4 – Base Color / None

### 4. Matching / Fabric Width
For a single base (garment) color, the user can define fabric widths based on Match Types and Material Colors. In this combination, the user can also add the fabric consumption and price.
Figure 5 – Matching / Fabric Width

### 5. Matching / Table Represent
The user can define different consumption and price values for each combination of Match Type, Material Color, and Material Size, for the given garment size and garment color.
Figure 6 – Matching / Table

### 6. Matching / None
The user can define fabric width and price for different Match Types and Material Colors, with no dependency on garment size.
Figure 7 – Matching / None

### 7. Body Type / Fabric Width
The user can define fabric width and price by Body Types for the garment colors. In this combination, the user can also add the fabric consumption and price.
Figure 8 – Body Type / Fabric Width

### 8. Body Type / Table
The user can define a different fabric width and price for each combination of Body Type and Material Size for garment color and garment sizes.
Figure 9 – Body Type / Table

### 9. Body Type / None
The user can define fabric width and price for different Body Types, with no dependency on garment size.
Figure 10 – Body Type / None

### 10. Table / Base Size
The user can define fabric width and price for every combination of Material Color and garment Size (Base Size), giving a full color-by-size table.
Figure 11 – Table / Base Size

### 11. Table / Fabric Width
The user can define fabric width for every Material Color, for the garment sizes. In this combination, the user can also add the fabric consumption and price.
Figure 12 – Table / Fabric Width

### 12. Table / Table
The user can define fabric width and price for every combination of Material Color and Material Size. This is the most granular option, producing a full color x size x width matrix.
Figure 13 – Table / Table

### 13. Table / None
The user can define consumption and price for each Material Color, with no dependency on garment size.
Figure 14 – Table / None

### 14. None / Base Size
There is no color dependency, so a single fabric applies to all garment colors. Consumption and price are defined against each garment size (Base Size).
Figure 15 – None / Base Size

### 15. None / Fabric Width
There is no color dependency. Single Fabric width are defined against each color/Size of garment. In this combination, the user can also add the fabric consumption and price.
Figure 16 – None / Fabric Width

### 16. None / Table
There is no color dependency. Consumption and price are defined by Material Size in a table for garment sizes, applicable uniformly across all garment colors.
Figure 17 – None / Table

### 17. None / None
There is no color or size dependency. A single consumption and price value applies uniformly to the entire garment, regardless of color or size.
No screenshot was included for this combination in the source document.

### NOTE: The Matching, Body Type, and Fabric Width dependencies are enabled for entering fabric consumption and price only when the Base Colorways option is enabled in the Techpack.

### Using Sizes Groups
In this mode, sizes will be replaced with Sizes groups selected in style. And it should enable when the toggle button is on.
Figure 18 – Size group Screen

### Scenario Planner:
In garment manufacturing, fabric procurement is not always uniform across all garment sizes. Different garment sizes may require different fabric widths, consumption rates, and fabric prices.
Additionally, the same garment size may also be planned under multiple procurement scenarios. This may occur when the buyer wants to procure the same size using different fabric widths, suppliers, or pricing strategies to optimize cost, improve fabric utilization, or accommodate production requirements.
The Scenario Planner enables users to create multiple procurement scenarios for a single BOM row without splitting the BOM.
The system then calculates the fabric requirement for each scenario independently and consolidates the total procurement requirement.
Example

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 2 rows · columns: Scenario (text), Sizes (text), Width (text), Consumption (text), Order Qty (integer)]
| Scenario | Sizes | Width | Consumption | Order Qty |
| Scenario 1 | S, M, L, XL | 54 Inch | 1.20 Mtr | 4,000 |
| Scenario 2 | XL, XXL | 56 Inch | 1.40 Mtr | 2,600 |
Or even:

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 2 rows · columns: Scenario (text), Size (text), Color (text), Width (text), Consumption (text)]
| Scenario | Size | Color | Width | Consumption |
| Scenario 1 | XL | Navy | 54 Inch | 1.20 Mtr |
| Scenario 2 | XL | Black | 56 Inch | 1.35 Mtr |
In this example, the same garment size (XL) is procured under two different scenarios because the procurement requirements differ by color and fabric width.

### Controls & Validations:
• System should restrict consumption specification in multiple line for same garment sizes.
• System should highlight consumption difference between width is more than 20%. This should be an alert only.
• System should show alert if consumption for fabric material is more than 5. This should also be an alert only.
• TBA quantity requirement will be handled by using consumption. In case user enters consumption against multiple widths of fabric for same color, system will popup alert that you have entered TBA quantity consumption multiple times.

##### Price List handling
• In case price list is enabled, then system should auto populate price of respective material color and width based on price list.
• In case price list doesn’t have price for a material color & size then:
• In case color price is missing=> system should bring lowest color price of respective material
• In case width price is missing=> system should bring lowest color size price of respective material. In absence of size, system should bring lowest color price.
• In case material price is not available and price list enforced for that material system should populate price as zero.
Wastage% to be discussed with product team.

### Change in Price Request
In case price request is practiced, then system will show above BOM line link on Price Request Line as well.
If user clicks and open above grid in case of price request, then other values in the new consumption & price request screen will be read-only. Sourcing team will not be able to make any changes in consumptions and material attributes. Option to define price on Material Request line under above screen will also become read only.

## Specification: Color Dependency & Size Dependency Handling

### Objective
Control how Material Color and Material Size (Roll Width) behave against garment attributes while allowing users to create new Material Colors and Material Sizes directly from the same page.

# 1. Color Dependency

## Available Options

### A. Base Color
Behavior
• One row per Garment Color.
• Material Color = Garment Color automatically.
• Material Color field is read-only.
• No duplicate color rows allowed.
• User cannot manually select Material Color.
Example

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 2 rows · columns: Garment Color (text), Material Color (text)]
| Garment Color | Material Color |
| Red | Red (Auto) |
| Black | Black (Auto) |

### B. Table Color
Behavior
• User manually selects Material Color.
• Multiple Material Colors allowed for same Garment Color.
• Multiple rows allowed for the same Garment Color.
• User can create a new Material Color directly from dropdown.
Example

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 3 rows · columns: Garment Color (text), Material Color (text)]
| Garment Color | Material Color |
| Red | Scarlet Red |
| Red | Dark Red |
| Red | Burgundy |

### C. None
Behavior
• Material Color not required.
• Material Color column disabled or hidden.
• Single row per Garment Color.

# 2. Material Color Dropdown

## Standard Values
Red
Black
Navy
White
Grey

### Last Dropdown Option
+ Add New Material Color

### User Flow
• User opens Material Color dropdown.
• Selects:
+ Add New Material Color
• Popup shown:
Enter Material Color:
• User enters:
Burgundy
• System:
• Adds Burgundy to Material Color master list.
• Updates dropdown immediately.
• Selects Burgundy for current row.
• Makes Burgundy available in all other rows.

# 3. Size Dependency
(Material Size = Roll Width)

## A. Base Size

### Behavior
Material Size automatically follows Garment Size.
No manual Roll Width selection.
Example:

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 3 rows · columns: Garment Size (text), Material Size (text)]
| Garment Size | Material Size |
| XS | XS |
| S | S |
| M | M |
Material Size field is read-only.

## B. Table Size

### Behavior
User selects Roll Width manually.
Multiple Roll Width rows allowed per color.
Example

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 3 rows · columns: Garment Color (text), Roll Width (text)]
| Garment Color | Roll Width |
| Red | 54 INCH |
| Red | 56 INCH |
| Red | 58 INCH |
User can add new width directly from dropdown.

## C. None

### Behavior
Material Size not required.
Roll Width column hidden or disabled.
Consumption entered without size mapping.

# 4. Material Size (Roll Width) Dropdown

## Standard Values
54 INCH
56 INCH
58 INCH
60 INCH

### Last Dropdown Option
+ Add New Material Size
or
+ Add New Roll Width

## User Flow
• User opens Roll Width dropdown.
• Selects:
+ Add New Roll Width
• Popup appears:
Enter Roll Width:
• User enters:
62 INCH
• System:
• Adds 62 INCH to width master list.
• Makes it available globally.
• Automatically selects it for the current row.

# 5. Validation Rules

### Material Color
• Value cannot be blank when Color Dependency = Table.
• Newly added value must be unique.
• Duplicate names not allowed.
Example:
Red
RED
red
Should be treated as same value.

### Material Size / Roll Width
• Value cannot be blank when Size Dependency = Table.
• Newly added width must be unique.
• Duplicate widths not allowed.
Example:
56 INCH
56 inch
56 Inch
Should be treated as one value.

# 6. UI Requirements

### Remove
❌ Add Garment Color button
❌ Add Garment Size button

### Keep
✅ Material Color dropdown
✅ Material Size (Roll Width) dropdown
✅ "+ Add New Material Color"
✅ "+ Add New Roll Width"
✅ Color Dependency selector
✅ Size Dependency selector

# Expected Result
Users cannot create new Garment Colors or Garment Sizes, but they can create and use new Material Colors and Material Sizes (Roll Widths) directly from the respective dropdowns without leaving the page.

### Change in Material Consumption Request
In case of consumption request, same link be available on respective material consumption request line. User will not be able to specify or change price if already updated.

### Change In Material Code Request
While creating Material code request from, user will be able to select Fabric Name’s system coding fields’ values. These values will be just for reference only. There will be no impact otherwise.

##### Material Code Request

##### Request Screen
In request screen, system will show fields below fields as Text field where user will be able to enter value if required. These fields will auto populate based on Fabric Article Name coding defined in the system for respective material type.
These fields will be visible to sourcing team while linking material code to the request.
